english.title: Possess forged / counterfeit goods for export / import - evade prohibition / restriction / defraud His Majesty
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) knowingly acquired possession of goods, namely **(..SPECIFY THE NATURE OF THE FORGED OR COUNTERFEIT ITEMS..), with respect to the

(A)_[exportation]_
(B)_[importation]_

of which a prohibition or restriction was for the time being in force with intent to

(C)_[defraud His Majesty of any duty payable on the goods]_
(D)_[evade any prohibition or restriction with respect to the goods]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 170(1)(a), (3) and (4A) of the Customs and Excise Management Act 1979.

english.notes:
(i) This offence wording may be used for an offence of possession in connection with a prohibition/restriction on the importation/exportation having effect by virtue of Section 20 or 21 of the Forgery and Counterfeiting Act 1981.
(ii) See section 171 for general provisions as to offences and penalties.
(iii) See section 49 for forfeiture provisions
(iv) Section 10 of the Interpretation Act 1978 states that any reference to the Sovereign reigning at the time of the passing of the Act is to be construed, unless the contrary intention appears, as a reference to the Sovereign for the time being. As such, references to ‘Her Majesty’ and ‘the Queen’ have been replaced in the wording of the offences to state ‘His Majesty’ or ‘the King’, although this may not be the strict wording of the legislation.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine of £20,000 or of three times the value of the goods, whichever is the greater.
INDICTMENT: Ten years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
